question: Will Flávio Bolsonaro finish in second place in the first round of the 2026 Brazilian presidential election?
resolution_criteria:
A presidential election is scheduled to take place in Brazil on October 4, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the listed candidate who receives the second-most valid votes in the first round of this election.

The named candidates will be primarily ranked by the number of valid votes received in the specified election. If two or more candidates are tied on valid votes, ties will be broken by alphabetical order of the candidates' last names. This market will resolve to the candidate that occupies the second-highest finishing position after applying this ranking.

If the result of this election isn't known definitively by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/).
research:
I couldn't open any pages directly because the proxy refused every fetch (Wikipedia, Gazeta do Povo, CNN Brasil, the market aggregators). Everything below comes from search-result snippets, so check the key numbers before relying on them. Some search results also included material dated after 2026-09-22. I ignored all of it.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on the official first-round results from the TSE (dadosabertos.tse.jus.br) or a consensus of credible reporting. The first round is on 2026-10-04. As of 2026-09-22 no votes have been cast, so the TSE has no results to show. I could not fetch the TSE site.
- The rule only counts the listed candidate in second place by valid votes. Flávio does not resolve "Yes" if he finishes first or third.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. In every September poll I found, Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) is second behind Lula (PT), and he leads the third-placed candidate, Augusto Cury, by more than 20 points. So the realistic way this fails is Flávio finishing **first**, not falling to third. The Lula-Flávio gap is about 2 to 8 points, depending on the poll.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- Mid-Sept 2026 (exact dates unconfirmed): the Portuguese Wikipedia poll table lists Datafolha (fieldwork Sept 15-16), Quaest (Sept 17-20) and AtlasIntel (Sept 11-16). The snippet was garbled. Read as Lula vs Flávio, the figures are roughly 44-44, 39-35 and 45.6-37.8, but the columns could not be confirmed. [pt.wikipedia](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pesquisas_de_opini%C3%A3o_para_a_elei%C3%A7%C3%A3o_presidencial_no_Brasil_em_2026)
- Sept 2026 (date unconfirmed): an AtlasIntel first-round poll had Lula 46.3% and Flávio 43.9%. [Gazeta do Povo](https://www.gazetadopovo.com.br/eleicoes/2026/pesquisa-eleitoral-2026/atlasintel-presidente-setembro-2026-3/)
- ~2026-09-02: Quaest, its first poll of the official campaign: Lula 37%, Flávio 30%, Cury 10%, Renan Santos 3%; Caiado, Zema and Marçal 1% each. Runoff: Lula 42%, Flávio 41%. [Gazeta do Povo](https://www.gazetadopovo.com.br/eleicoes/2026/pesquisa-eleitoral-2026/quaest-presidente-setembro-2026/)
- 2026-09-01 to 03 (fieldwork): Datafolha: Lula 38%, Flávio 33%, Cury 8%, Caiado 4%, Renan Santos 3%. [CNN Brasil](https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/eleicoes/datafolha-no-1o-turno-lula-tem-38-flavio-33-e-cury-8/)
- ~2026-08-31 / 09-01: Real Time Big Data had Lula 38, Flávio 30, Cury 11. BTG/Nexus had 39/33/11. AtlasIntel/Bloomberg had 43.4/33.7/7.8. [Congresso em Foco](https://www.congressoemfoco.com.br/noticia/121834/augusto-cury-cresce-e-aparece-em-3-na-pesquisa-real-time-big-data)
- 2026-03: Datafolha had a runoff technical tie, Lula 46 to Flávio 43, with Lula leading every first-round scenario. [Yahoo/Reuters](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/flavio-bolsonaro-draws-even-lula-161733328.html)
- 2025-12-06: Flávio launched his candidacy with his father's endorsement. [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/12/6/flavio-bolsonaro-enters-brazils-2026-presidential-race-with-fathers-nod)

## 4. Base rates
- Since 2006, every Brazilian first round has been a two-way contest, with third place far behind. That fits the current polls, where third place is around 10%.
- Main risk to "Yes": a polling error on the first-place margin.
  - In 2022, final polls had Lula ahead by a wide margin (Datafolha about 14 points among valid votes). The result was Lula 48.4%, Bolsonaro 43.2%: the right-wing candidate beat his polls by several points.
  - In 2018, Jair Bolsonaro came first in round one.
  - This is from my background knowledge, not a source I fetched.
- In the polls above, the Lula-Flávio gap ranges from about 0 to 8 points across pollsters, with AtlasIntel and Datafolha tighter in mid-September. A gap of this size is within a 2022-sized polling error.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Polymarket "Flávio Bolsonaro 2nd in first round":
  - About 70% in April 2026 (one April 2 listing showed $0.60, conflicting with a 72% figure in the same article's header). [Lines](https://www.lines.com/prediction-markets/elections/brazil-presidential-election-first-round-2nd-place)
  - About 62% on 2026-05-18. [Orrery](https://www.orrery.me/markets/will-flvio-bolsonaro-finish-in-second-place-in-the-first-round-of-the-2026-brazilian-presidential-election)
- Kalshi equivalent (KXBRPRESIDENT2): about 51 on 2026-05-28. [SimpleFunctions](https://simplefunctions.dev/api/public/market/KXBRPRESIDENT2-BRPRES26-2-FBOL)
- A snippet from a September 2026 analysis said Flávio's probability of finishing second fell 13 points while Lula's rose 15, which suggests the market moved toward Flávio finishing first. I could not see the date or the source. [Octagon](https://www.octagonai.co/markets/politics/brazil/brazil-presidential-election-first-round-2nd-place/)
- I could not find a Polymarket or Kalshi price dated close to 2026-09-22.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Final Datafolha, Quaest and AtlasIntel polls are expected in late September and early October. I found nothing dated after the cutoff that I could use.
- The final TV debates are customarily held in the days before the vote (traditionally TV Globo around Oct 1-2). I did not confirm the 2026 schedule.
- First round: 2026-10-04, with the TSE count the same night. A runoff is expected if no one gets more than 50% of valid votes.
- Watch tactical voting: Cury's and Caiado's voters moving to Flávio could push him into first.

forecasts.reasoning:
- Quaest (around Sept 2) had Lula 37, Flávio 30.
  - Datafolha (Sept 1-3) had 38 to 33.
  - AtlasIntel/Bloomberg (around Sept 1) had 43.4 to 33.7.
  - Mid-September AtlasIntel readings still show Lula ahead, at 46.3 to 43.9, or 45.6 to 37.8 by another reading.
  - Third place, at about 10%, is far behind, so finishing third is a negligible risk.
- **For No:**
  - Mid-September polls look tighter. A garbled snippet may show Datafolha at 44 to 44.
  - In 2022, Bolsonaro beat his final polls by several points.
  - Cury's and Caiado's voters (about 12 to 15%) could vote tactically for Flávio.
  - An undated market snippet says Flávio's "2nd place" probability fell 13 points, which suggests the market sees a growing chance he finishes first.
  - Kalshi priced Yes at about 51 in late May.

(e) **Scenarios.**
- **No:** Right-leaning voters consolidate behind Flávio in the final week. The polls understate the right as they did in 2022, and Flávio edges Lula, say 45 to 44.
- **Yes:** Lula keeps a 3 to 6 point lead. Cury holds most of his vote, Flávio finishes a strong second, and the race goes to a runoff.

(f) **From base rate to final.** I started around 67%.
- I moved down about 8 points because the race tightened in mid-September.
- I moved down slightly more for the documented pro-right polling bias and the market signal pointing toward Flávio finishing first.
- I moved partly back up because most pollsters still show Lula ahead.

That leaves me at about 58%.

Probability: 58%

- For Yes:
  - Quaest, Sept 17-20: Lula 39, Flávio 35.
  - AtlasIntel, Sept 11-16: about 45.6 to 37.8.
  - Early September: Datafolha 38-33, Quaest 37-30, BTG/Nexus 39-33. Lula leads consistently.
- For No:
  - Datafolha, Sept 15-16: possibly 44-44.
  - An AtlasIntel September poll: 46.3 vs 43.9.
  - In 2022 the polls missed the Bolsonaro vote by several points.
  - An undated September market analysis showed Flávio's probability of finishing second falling 13 points while Lula's rose 15. That suggests the market sees a real chance of Flávio finishing first.
  - Polymarket priced Yes at about 62% in May, and Kalshi at about 51 in late May.

**(e) Scenarios**
- No: Late tactical voting moves Cury and Caiado voters to Flávio, and a 2022-style polling miss repeats. Flávio wins the first round by 1-2 points.
- Yes: Lula's Northeast base and his incumbency hold, as the polls show. Lula leads by 3-6 points and Flávio finishes a clear second.

**(f) From base rate to final probability**
I start at about 70%, given that the poll leader usually holds a 4-5 point lead. I then move down about 12 points for three reasons:
- the 2022 precedent of the right-wing candidate being underestimated;
- a likely squeeze of third-party voters toward the anti-PT frontrunner;
- the narrowing mid-September Datafolha and AtlasIntel numbers, along with signs that the market shifted toward Flávio finishing first.

I add 1-2% of residual risk from a third-place finish or other outcomes.

Probability: 57%

2 to 8 points. In tight races, the right has beaten its polls (2018, and 2022 by about 5 points on the margin). For a lead of about 4 to 5 points with polling error of about 5 points, a reasonable base rate is around 70%.

(d) **Strongest evidence.**
- **For Yes:**
  - Datafolha, September 1-3: Lula 38, Flávio 33.
  - Quaest, around September 2: Lula 37, Flávio 30.
  - AtlasIntel/Bloomberg, late August: Lula 43.4, Flávio 33.7.
  - Quaest, September 17-20: roughly 39-35.
  - Third place, at about 10%, is irrelevant.
- **For No:**
  - Mid-September tightening: AtlasIntel at 46.3 vs 43.9, and possibly a Datafolha tie around 44-44 (garbled snippet).
  - The 2022 precedent of the right outperforming its polls.
  - A September market snippet suggesting traders moved toward Flávio finishing first.
  - Cury and Caiado voters could consolidate behind Flávio.

(e) **Scenarios.**
- **No:** Late consolidation of right-wing voters plus a 2022-style polling miss, and Flávio edges Lula 45-44 in the first round.
- **Yes:** Lula holds a 3 to 6 point lead, roughly matching the polls, and Flávio finishes a comfortable second.

(f) **From base rate to final probability.** I start at about 70%. The polls are tightening into mid-September, AtlasIntel (the most accurate pollster in 2022) shows a narrow gap, and the market signal points toward Flávio finishing first. For these reasons I move down to about 60 to 63%. Earlier market prices of 51 to 62% support a figure in this range.

Probability: 61%
